proposed_fixes.title: Verify Unicode apply results before advancing displayed names
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A shell-apply failure may be hidden by optimistic item-state updates and unchecked execution results. Saved regex state differs from the literal report, so the exact trigger remains unconfirmed and U+A789 handling is not proven faulty.
plan: Reproduce literal U+2014 to U+A789+space replacement and the archived capture-group regex on unique synthetic files/folders; compare actual directory names by code point, not just preview.
Use the captured reproduction to inspect RenameItem/PerformOperations and operation-aborted/per-item outcomes; preserve native shell undo, collision and nested-folder behavior.
If disk apply fails while preview succeeds, update item names/paths only from confirmed successful outcomes and retain failed rows with a useful error instead of assuming the planned name is real.
Reuse applicable failure-handling ideas/tests from closed-unmerged #47060 after maintainer review; do not reopen or duplicate its implementation blindly.
If only the regex/settings combination fails, fix that confirmed matching/state path instead of adding a Unicode-specific workaround.
verification: For files and folders containing an interior em dash, both preview and disk names contain the exact intended U+A789 then U+0020 sequence.
Test literal and saved-regex modes separately, with and without enumeration, and keep-UI-open versus closing after Apply.
A forced shell rename failure does not display a nonexistent successful name; unaffected items, undo and nested-folder paths remain correct.

confidence.rationale: The apply/state hazard is visible in current source and fits the UI/disk discrepancy, but the actual HRESULT and the exact literal-versus-regex trigger are missing; it is not a confirmed Unicode root cause.

comment.body:
Thanks for the detailed steps and the report ZIP. The saved last-run state in that report uses `(\d)—([A-Za-z])` with `$1꞉ $2`, and its saved flags include regular expressions, whereas the steps describe searching for the em dash alone. These may simply be different attempts.

Could you share one non-sensitive filename before the failing attempt, its expected name, and its actual name afterward, together with a screenshot of the search/replacement fields and regex, occurrence and enumeration toggles used for that same attempt? Please also indicate whether Apply left the PowerRename window open. You can type a synthetic example or upload through the GitHub web UI with personal content hidden. This distinguishes a matching/settings issue from a shell operation that updates the preview but not the file; the existing ZIP and Windows/version details do not need to be sent again.

reproduce.title: Compare literal and saved-regex Unicode rename on disk
reproduce.version_requirement: 0.102.2933 and current release as a comparison
prerequisites: Use disposable test data; preserve existing user configuration
setup: Prepare unique disposable files named 1—Alpha.txt and 2—Beta.txt and a folder named 3—Gamma.
Keep the replacement characters literal: U+A789 followed by U+0020; do not substitute ASCII colon.
The reporter's ∥ is explanatory concatenation notation, not an additional replacement character.
steps: 1. With regex off, replace U+2014 with U+A789 plus space, Filename only, using the reported include/enumeration controls; record preview and actual names.
2. Restore the disposable names and repeat with the archived regex (\d)—([A-Za-z]), replacement $1꞉ $2 and saved flags 0xCF.
3. Repeat with enumeration off and compare keeping the window open versus closing it after Apply; independently inspect the actual filesystem names/code points.
4. If preview and disk diverge, capture shell-operation result/aborted state in a maintainer debug session and compare with a deliberately locked target before selecting a patch.
reproduce.expected_result: Matching inputs receive the intended literal Unicode name on disk. Any failed operation remains visibly failed; preview and model state must not claim nonexistent filenames.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Create a disposable test directory with the three synthetic names and record the Unicode code points before and after each separate literal/regex trial. Do not use the reporter's private files.

fix_assessment.rationale: A conditional apply-result/state correction is plausible. #47060 is closed/unmerged and not established coverage of this report; no active covering implementation was identified.
